question: When can failsafe be disabled during return to home on the Matrice 30T?

intake.decided_by: code (single pass has no intake call)

brief.short_answer: The sources do not authorize disabling failsafe during a return-to-home. The DJI Matrice 30T allows configuring the loss-of-remote-control action (RTH, land, or hover) but does not describe a method to disable failsafe altogether. In practice, loss of signal leads to the configured action, with RTH being common, and RTH behavior is discussed in the context of lighting, GNSS, and battery considerations in the manuals. Incident reports show lost-link triggers RTH; there is no evidence in the sources that disables are allowed during RTH.

claims.text: FAA guidance discusses loss of control link procedures and pre-determined procedures for loss of control link, including trying to reestablish control and starting emergency or contingency procedures.
claims.quote: If connection cannot be reestablished, start emergency or contingency procedures for loss of control link.

claims.text: No specific time interval exists for interruption of VLOS and there is no described mechanism to disable fail-safe during RTH; if VLOS cannot be regained, pre-determined procedures for loss of VLOS should be followed, including potential RTH or other actions.
claims.quote: For this reason, no specific time interval exists in which interruption of VLOS is permissible... If the remote PIC cannot regain VLOS, the remote PIC or person manipulating the controls should follow pre-determined procedures for the loss of VLOS.

claims.text: The action of the aircraft when the remote controller signal is lost can be set to RTH, land, or hover in DJI Pilot 2.
claims.quote: The action of the aircraft when the remote controller signal is lost can be set to RTH, land, or hover in Camera View > > > Signal Lost Action in DJI Pilot 2 .

claims.text: During RTH, the lighting conditions and vision systems affect whether failsafe RTH activates and how it proceeds; if lighting is insufficient or vision systems are unavailable, the RTH behavior changes (Original Route RTH, etc.).
claims.quote: The RTH altitude is related to the Home Point... The aircraft cannot avoid obstacles during failsafe RTH when there is insufficient light. Exit RTH and use the remote controller to control the aircraft when the remote controller signal is normal.

claims.text: Incident report notes a loss of link and automatic RTH behavior, with RTH at programmed altitude and later observation of interference affecting the flight controller.
claims.quote: Lost link and RTH occurred twice on back-to-back hops. After securing flights; the crew noticed a cellular antenna booster... interference with the flight controller

claims.text: Other incident report describes loss of control inputs and subsequent RTH not responding initially, later regaining control and landing; this illustrates RTH behavior but does not indicate any option to disable failsafe.
claims.quote: The drone tried to initiate RTH but did not respond; after troubleshooting, control was regained and the drone landed.

claims.text: Forum post describes an M30T flight where the aircraft entered return to home with video view intact and stick inputs non-responsive; no definitive cause or disablement instruction is given.
claims.quote: The aircraft entered return to home. The pilot could still see the live video but stick inputs had no effect, and the aircraft landed at its home point.

gaps.text: No explicit statement allowing disabling of failsafe during RTH is provided.
No clear rule on whether failsafe can be disabled during RTH specifically for Matrice 30T.
How disabling interacts with original route vs advanced RTH modes under varying lighting/visibility is not fully defined.
